annotation_description: Willowrush Verge on turn 1 with no Forest/Island in play only produces {U}, preventing the turn 1 Gene Pollinator ({G}) cast. Botanical Sanctum enters untapped when you control ≤2 other lands and produces both {G} and {U}, enabling the turn 1 Gene Pollinator.

Casting a second creature (Hired Claw) in the precombat main phase when holding multiple combat tricks (Turn Inside Out, Full Bore, Might of the Meek) is suboptimal. The player should attack first with the existing Hired Claw to trigger its 'whenever you attack with one or more Lizards' ability for 1 damage, then potentially use combat tricks if needed. Deploying the second Hired Claw before combat gives the opponent information and doesn't help this turn's attack since the new creature has summoning sickness. More importantly, the player is tapping their only Mountain to cast the creature, leaving no mana open for combat tricks during the attack step. They could have attacked with the existing Hired Claw first (dealing 1 damage via trigger), then cast the second Hired Claw post-combat.

Casting Might of the Meek in precombat main phase instead of during combat or after attackers. This gives the opponent unnecessary information and a window to respond before attacks. The opponent has Gene Pollinator and Botanical Sanctum representing potential mana for interaction. The player should attack first with both Hired Claws (triggering the Hired Claw ability for 1 damage), then cast the cantrip during combat or post-combat.

Fetched Gene Pollinator instead of Llanowar Elves. Gene Pollinator requires tapping itself AND another permanent to produce mana, while Llanowar Elves taps alone for {G}. With Spider Manifestation (costs {1}{R/G}) and other spells in hand needing mana, Llanowar Elves provides more efficient ramp.

Leyline of Resonance costs 2RR which is expensive, but with only 1 Mountain and 2 Hired Claws (which likely produce red mana when tapped), it could potentially be cast in a turn or two. More importantly, Leyline of Resonance has incredible synergy with this deck - it copies any instant/sorcery targeting a single creature you control. With 3 Slickshot Show-Offs and 3 Turn Inside Outs plus Full Bore, Leyline would double all combat tricks AND each copy would trigger Slickshot's +2/+0 ability again. This creates massive burst damage potential. However, at 2RR with only 1 Mountain currently, it may be too slow. A third Turn Inside Out could be the discard instead since having 3 copies is redundant, but the Leyline's ceiling is much higher if it resolves.

At 9 life facing two Hired Claws, the player cast Spider Manifestation (a 2/2 for 2 mana) before playing their land drop for the turn. They have Forest and Willowrush Verge in hand with 0 land drops used. Playing a land first is better sequencing - it preserves mana options and doesn't cost anything. Additionally, casting Mockingbird copying a Gene Pollinator (or even Spider Manifestation after casting it) could have been considered to ramp faster. More importantly, the player should have played their land first before casting any spells to maximize available mana for the rest of the turn.

Gem25F Gramps declined to cast Mockingbird, which could copy Spider Manifestation (a 2/2 with reach and mana ability) for X=2 (3 mana total). With Botanical Sanctum, two Willowrush Verges, and two Gene Pollinators available for mana, they had plenty of resources to cast it. At 9 life facing two Hired Claws that deal extra damage on attack, developing the board is critical. A flying copy of Spider Manifestation would provide both an attacker and a blocker. Additionally, Nature's Rhythm could be cast from the graveyard via Harmonize, potentially tutoring a powerful creature to stabilize. Passing on both options wastes mana and tempo in a losing position.

DSV3 Spike has the opponent at 9 life with two Hired Claws on board and a hand full of pump spells (3x Turn Inside Out, Full Bore, 3x Slickshot Show-Off). Instead of casting Slickshot Show-Off normally (which has haste and would allow attacking this turn), they chose to plot it, delaying it to a future turn. With 2 Mountains available, casting Slickshot Show-Off for {1}{R} puts a hasty flyer on board immediately. Attacking with both Hired Claws and Slickshot Show-Off would deal 2 damage from Hired Claw triggers + at least 1 from Slickshot (more with pump spells next turn or even this turn if they sequence correctly). Plotting wastes the haste ability and delays pressure against an opponent who is deploying blockers including Spider Manifestation with reach.

Player incorrectly believed they had no blue mana available, but both Willowrush Verges can tap for U since they control a Forest. At 6 life facing two Hired Claws (which deal bonus damage via lizard attack triggers), an additional blocker is critical for survival. Mockingbird could have been cast for X=2-3 to copy a creature, while still potentially holding up Spider-Sense via web-slinging (returning a tapped creature to cast for just U).

DSV3 Spike had lethal on board. Opponent is at 6 life. Attacking with both Hired Claws and Slickshot Show-Off would deal 2 damage from Hired Claw triggers, then casting any Turn Inside Out on Slickshot Show-Off (which also triggers Slickshot's +2/+0) would give massive flying damage - even one spell makes Slickshot a 6/2 flyer, totaling 10+ damage against 6 life. Instead, DSV3 Spike passed without casting spells or attacking, letting the opponent untap and attack them.

DSV3 Spike missed lethal damage. With Gem25F Gramps at 6 life, casting even one Turn Inside Out on the flying Slickshot Show-Off would make it a 6/2 (1+3 from Turn Inside Out +2 from Slickshot's noncreature spell trigger), dealing exactly 6 damage through the air with no flyers to block. Additional Hired Claw triggers and attacks would have added even more damage.

At 6 life facing lethal pressure from two Hired Claws (2 damage from triggers alone per attack) and a flying Slickshot Show-Off, Gramps passed without casting Mockingbird. A flying blocker copying Slickshot Show-Off (MV 2, so X=2, costing 3 mana total) would provide a crucial flying blocker while still potentially leaving mana for Spider-Sense via web-slinging. Without a blocker for the Slickshot, the opponent can freely attack with flying + pump spells for lethal.

DSV3 Spike is at 11 life, opponent is at 3 life. Both Hired Claws are tapped (they attacked), and Slickshot Show-Off is tapped (it attacked). DSV3 Spike has untapped Mountains and Fire Nation Palace. The Hired Claw ability says '{1}{R}: Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature. Activate only if an opponent lost life this turn and only once each turn.' The opponent did lose life this turn (went from 6 to 3), so both Hired Claws can be activated to grow. But more critically, the opponent is at 3 life and DSV3 Spike has burn/pump spells in hand but no untapped attackers to target meaningfully for additional damage this combat. However, looking more carefully: Hired Claw has the triggered ability 'Whenever you attack with one or more Lizards, this creature deals 1 damage to target opponent' - both Hired Claws trigger, dealing 2 damage total. The opponent went from some life total to 3. Next turn, attacking with both Hired Claws would deal 2 (from triggers) + combat damage, easily killing the opponent at 3 life. But wait - the opponent has Gene Pollinators (1/2s) that could block. The key question is whether DSV3 Spike could have won THIS turn. With the opponent at 3 life after combat damage, and having Full Bore ({R}: +3/+2) and Turn Inside Out ({R}: +3/+0) in hand, plus 4 untapped lands producing red mana - but all creatures are tapped from attacking. There's no way to deal damage with pump spells on tapped creatures outside of combat. So passing seems reasonable... unless Fire Nation Palace's firebending ability could help, but that requires an attacking creature. Actually, re-reading: the opponent is at 3 life. DSV3 Spike passed without activating Hired Claw's +1/+1 counter ability. Both Hired Claws attacked, the opponent lost life, so the condition is met. Activating both Hired Claws ({1}{R} each) would make them 2/3s, which is relevant for getting through blockers next turn. With 3 untapped Mountains and Fire Nation Palace, DSV3 Spike has enough mana for at least one activation. Missing these activations when the opponent is at 3 life and has blockers available is a meaningful mistake.

At 3 life facing lethal on board (two Hired Claws deal 2 damage from triggers alone when attacking, plus combat damage), Gem25F Gramps declined to cast Mockingbird which could copy Spider Manifestation to create another blocker. With 8 lands/mana sources available, they could cast Mockingbird for X=2 (3 mana total) to copy Spider Manifestation, getting a 2/2 reach creature that also taps for mana. This additional blocker could be critical for surviving the next attack. At 3 life, every body on the battlefield matters for blocking, and passing with mana available and a creature in hand is wasteful when you're about to die.

DSV3 Spike is at 11 life with the opponent at 3 life. The Slickshot Show-Off attacked this turn (it's tapped), and now in postcombat main, Spike has Full Bore and three Turn Inside Outs in hand with untapped Mountains and Fire Nation Palace. While there are no untapped creatures to target with pump spells right now (Slickshot and both Hired Claws are tapped), the decision to pass is technically correct since pump spells need a valid attack to matter. However, Spike could consider plotting a Slickshot Show-Off from hand (paying 1R) to set up a devastating next turn with plotted Slickshot + pump spells for lethal through the Spider Manifestation blocker. With opponent at 3 life, maximizing next turn's damage potential is critical. That said, the opponent has Spider-Sense potential (U open) and Spider Manifestation as a blocker with reach, so plotting to set up a bigger next turn could be the right call. Passing without plotting is slightly suboptimal.
